text: Saturn, when he assumes the dominion of the soul, makes his subjects, in his proper condition, sedate, austere, of seemingly simple manners, but really of a malignant temper; close, laborious, set on accomplishing their wants; constant in pursuing their object; persevering, exact, frugal, and retentive of property to a fault.

Jupiter, when ruling the soul, makes his subjects magnanimous, beneficent, courteous, devout, just, high-minded, liberal, and discreetly judicious in the direction of all matters; pious, of skilful conduct in business, lovers of their kindred and friends, equitable, humane, and bounteous.
Mars, when sole governor of the soul, and placed with dignity, makes his subjects noble, commanding, irascible, martial, versatile, powerful, daring, hasty, indifferent to consequences, and resolute.

Venus, when sole ruler of the soul, and posited honourably, makes her subjects amiable, gentle, elegant, fond of pleasure, social, of cheerful disposition, lovers of decency and the arts; fond of music, and of singing, and of feasting.

Mercury, when sole governor of the soul, makes his subjects wise, prudent, thoughtful, learned, ingenious, scientific, and disposed to research; busy in the pursuit of knowledge; discoverers and contrivers; given to investigation and to the study of nature.

The Moon, when sole ruler of the soul, and configurated with becoming dignity, renders her subjects of well-tempered disposition, of good memory, naturally social, well disposed to public life, lovers of conversation, ready in adapting themselves, easy in their address, and susceptible of impressions from others.

The Sun, when ruler of the soul and dignified, makes the native sedate, conscientious, of a noble nature, sociable, just, and lover of his kindred; one who acts uprightly, and who never forsakes the cause of right.
